title: Cannabis SMS Marketing: Compliance + Best Practices for 2026
summary: Texting is the highest-converting channel in cannabis retail, and the fastest way to land a TCPA lawsuit. Here's how to run SMS the right way.
body_text: Cannabis SMS marketing is the practice of sending promotional and transactional text messages to dispensary customers who have explicitly opted in to receive them. Because cannabis businesses are locked out of most paid social and search advertising, SMS is one of the few marketing channels a dispensary fully owns. It is also one of the most tightly regulated, with federal telemarketing law, mobile carrier policies, and state cannabis rules all stacked on top of each other. This guide breaks down the compliance rules that govern cannabis SMS as of August 2026, how to earn opt-in consent the right way, what you can and cannot say, how to choose a platform, and how to measure results, so you can build a text channel that drives repeat visits without putting the list at risk. In This Post Why SMS Works So Well for Dispensaries The Compliance Rules That Govern Cannabis SMS Consent and Opt-In: Building Your List the Right Way Content Rules: What You Can and Cannot Say Choosing an SMS Platform for Your Dispensary Measuring What Your Texts Actually Drive Getting Started with Cannabis SMS Marketing Common Questions Why SMS Works So Well for Dispensaries SMS is the highest-leverage owned channel most dispensaries have, because the people on the list already know you and asked to hear from you. Paid cannabis advertising is heavily restricted across most platforms, so the customers who opted in are gold. Texts reach them instantly, get read at far higher rates than email, and tie directly to a visit. Best of all, an opted-in list is an owned audience. No algorithm change or ad-policy update can take it away from you. For a dispensary, a healthy SMS list is one of the most durable marketing assets you can build. That durability is also why compliance matters so much: one careless blast can cost you the channel, or worse. The Compliance Rules That Govern Cannabis SMS Cannabis SMS sits under three overlapping layers of rules: federal telemarketing law, mobile carrier policies, and state cannabis marketing regulations. As of the writing of this article in August 2026, the practical requirements look like this, but every item below needs confirmation with counsel before you rely on it: TCPA (federal) . The Telephone Consumer Protection Act requires prior express written consent before sending marketing texts. Statutory damages run $500 per violation and up to $1,500 for willful or knowing violations, assessed per message, which is what makes a single non-compliant blast to a large list an existential number rather than a fine. Opt-out mechanics (federal, effective April 11, 2025). The FCC's consent revocation rules require senders to honor a revocation made through any reasonable means, treat the standard keywords (stop, quit, end, revoke, opt out, cancel, unsubscribe) as valid opt-outs, and process the request within 10 business days. One confirmatory text is permitted within five minutes, and it cannot contain promotional content. The portion of the rule that would make a single opt-out apply across every message type you send has been delayed again and is now scheduled to take effect in January 2027. Build for it now rather than retrofitting later. Quiet hours (federal). FCC rules restrict telephone solicitations before 8 a.m. and after 9 p.m. in the recipient's local time. Courts are currently split on whether a customer's opt-in also amounts to consent to receive messages inside those hours, and quiet-hours text claims have become an active class-action category. Until that question settles, send inside the window and consider adding time-of-day language to your opt-in terms. Carrier policies. The major carriers apply their own content rules on top of federal law, and cannabis sits on their restricted-content lists in most cases, alongside the categories the industry refers to as SHAFT. Enforcement happens at the brand level through A2P 10DLC campaign registration, not message by message, and it is a moving target. This is a core reason platform choice matters. State cannabis rules. Your state's cannabis marketing regulations govern promotions, product claims, discount language, and audience restrictions, and they differ meaningfully state to state. Treat compliance as the foundation, not an afterthought. The operators who win at SMS are the ones who treat the opt-in list as something to protect, not exhaust. Route your consent language, message templates, and sending practices through legal review before the first campaign goes out. Consent and Opt-In: Building Your List the Right Way Clear, documented, explicit opt-in consent is the non-negotiable starting point for cannabis SMS marketing. No buying lists, and no "we had their number anyway." Get explicit consent before texting anyone. Consent must be affirmative and documented, and your records should show when and how each customer opted in. Those records are your defense, so treat retention of them as part of the program. Honor opt-outs immediately and automatically. A "STOP" must work the first time, every time, without a human in the loop, and the other standard keywords have to work too. Federal rules give you 10 business days at the outside; a good platform does it instantly. Collect consent where customers already are. Checkout, your online menu, and loyalty sign-up are the natural moments to ask. Make the value clear at the moment you ask. "Get first access to drops and member deals" converts better than "join our texts." 💡 How Meadow handles this: Meadow's built-in loyalty program gives customers a concrete reason to opt in at sign-up, so list growth happens as a natural part of enrollment instead of a separate ask. See how dispensaries use their own data to level up loyalty . Content Rules: What You Can and Cannot Say What you send is regulated just as much as who you send it to. State cannabis rules constrain promotions, pricing language, and product claims, and carriers filter content on their own terms. Within those constraints, the messages that perform are the ones built around the customer: Lead with value. A real reason to come in beats "we exist." A restock of a customer's favorite, a member-only perk, an event, or early access gives people a reason that is actually about them. Tie offers to behavior. Win-back messages for lapsed buyers, early access for loyalty members, and category restocks for the people who buy that category. Mind timing and frequency. A few well-timed, relevant texts beat daily noise. Over-texting is the fastest way to drive opt-outs, and quiet-hours rules restrict late and early sends. Avoid health claims and restricted language. Most states prohibit therapeutic claims and regulate discount phrasing; run your message templates past compliance review. Carrier filtering applies to the words inside the message, not just who sends it. Cannabis terms in the text body can get a message filtered before it ever reaches a phone, and disguising those words with numbers or symbols in place of letters does not solve the problem. The same goes for links: dropping your store's website into the text can flag the message, because the destination identifies it as cannabis. It is worth being clear about what does not work here. Because carriers enforce at the brand level through 10DLC registration, misrepresenting your business type or rotating through new numbers when messages stop landing tends to make things worse, not better, and can get your brand blocked outright. The durable pattern is the opposite of evasion: register honestly, work with a platform that understands cannabis routing, keep the text itself short and neutral, and let a linked page carry the rich content. Meadow's Digital Flyers are built for exactly this: a short text links to a PIN-protected, branded page where you can share full offer details, product info, images, or a direct link to your menu, visible only to the customer who received it. If discounts are part of your SMS playbook, structure them deliberately rather than training customers to wait for blasts. Our guide to building a profitable dispensary discount strategy covers how to protect margin while still giving the list real value. Choosing an SMS Platform for Your Dispensary The right cannabis SMS platform handles compliance mechanics automatically and connects directly to your sales data. Evaluate on these criteria: Cannabis-friendly delivery. Can the platform actually deliver cannabis content reliably given carrier filtering, and can they explain how their routing and 10DLC registration work? Consent and opt-out automation. Opt-in records, automatic handling of every standard opt-out keyword, and quiet-hours enforcement should be built in, not manual. POS integration. Segmentation is only as good as the purchase data behind it. A platform that reads live sales data can target lapsed customers, VIPs, and category buyers precisely. Attribution. You should be able to trace a campaign to visits and revenue, not just delivery rates. 💡 How Meadow handles this: Text marketing is built directly into Meadow, so you can send targeted campaigns using segments from your live POS data, including purchase history, brand preference, and location, with compliant message templates included. See the power of marketing segments for how operators build them. For advanced multi-channel campaigns across SMS, email, and push, Meadow's Alpine IQ integration reads from the same source of truth, with customer records, purchase history, and marketing opt-ins syncing automatically between the two platforms. The Higher Path consolidated three separate systems into that setup; their story is here . Your POS is the data engine underneath all of this. If you are evaluating that layer too, start with the complete guide to choosing a cannabis dispensary POS system . Measuring What Your Texts Actually Drive Measure SMS campaigns by visits and revenue, not opens and deliveries. The point of a text is a customer through the door or an order placed, so the measurement loop has to connect campaigns back to sales. Track revenue per campaign, not just click or delivery rates. Watch opt-out rate as a health metric. A rising opt-out rate means you are spending the list faster than you are growing it. Watch delivery rate as a compliance signal. A sudden drop usually means carrier filtering, not customer disinterest, and it is worth diagnosing before you send again. Compare segments. If win-back messages outperform generic promos, shift the mix accordingly. 💡 How Meadow handles this: Because Meadow's customer data lives in the POS, you can see what a campaign actually drove in sales, closing the loop between a text sent and a customer through the door. Segments built from purchase history, including lapsed customers, VIPs, and category buyers, stay current automatically. Getting Started with Cannabis SMS Marketing A clear path from zero to a working, compliant SMS program: Run legal review first. Have counsel approve your consent language, opt-in flow, and message templates before anything sends. Set up consent capture at checkout, on your online menu, and in loyalty sign-up, with the value proposition stated at the moment of the ask. Choose a platform against the criteria above, with POS integration and compliance automation as requirements, not nice-to-haves. Start with one segmented campaign, such as a win-back message to customers who have not visited in 60 days, rather than a blast to everyone. Measure by revenue, iterate monthly, and keep the send frequency low enough that the opt-out rate stays flat. Customers who come in from a text still need a fast checkout when they arrive. If cash-only friction is costing you conversions, see our guide to accepting cashless payments at your dispensary . Ready to Text Smarter? See Why Operators Choose Meadow. Growing an SMS list shouldn't mean juggling spreadsheets and separate marketing tools. With Meadow, opt-in capture happens at loyalty sign-up, segments build themselves from live purchase data, and every campaign traces back to real revenue. We've been building cannabis retail software since 2014, and we've helped operators across six states turn their customer data into their best marketing channel. Yes, with consent. As of the writing of this article in August 2026, you must obtain prior express written consent before sending marketing texts, honor opt-outs made through any reasonable means, and follow TCPA, carrier, and state cannabis rules. Requirements change; confirm the current rules with counsel before launching. What are the TCPA penalties for a non-compliant text? Statutory damages are $500 per violation and up to $1,500 for a willful or knowing violation, assessed per message. On a list of any size, that arithmetic is the reason consent records and automatic opt-out handling are worth doing properly. What time of day can a dispensary send marketing texts? Federal rules restrict telephone solicitations before 8 a.m. and after 9 p.m. in the recipient's local time. As of August 2026, courts are split on whether an opt-in also covers messages inside those hours, and quiet-hours claims are an active litigation trend. Send inside the window, and confirm your approach with counsel. How often should a dispensary text customers? Prioritize relevance over frequency. A few well-timed, valuable messages outperform daily blasts, protect your opt-in list from churn, and keep your opt-out rate low. How do I build an SMS list for my dispensary? Collect opt-in consent at checkout, on your online menu, and through loyalty sign-up, and make the value clear at the moment you ask. Segment the list using your POS purchase data so each message is relevant to the person receiving it. What should I send in a cannabis SMS campaign? Value-led messages tied to behavior: restocks of favorites, member perks, events, early access, and win-back offers for lapsed customers. Avoid generic blasts and anything that conflicts with your state's content rules. Why are my dispensary's texts not getting delivered? Usually carrier filtering. Cannabis content is restricted on most carrier networks, enforcement happens at the brand level through 10DLC registration, and cannabis terms or a dispensary URL inside the message body can get it blocked. Keeping the text short and neutral, with the detail on a linked page, is the standard fix. Can I text customers about cannabis discounts? Usually yes with proper consent, but state rules on discount and promotional language vary and carriers filter cannabis content. Confirm your state's promotion rules with compliance counsel before sending discount campaigns.

title: Baird Medical and Alpmed Enter Strategic Partnership to Advance Irreversible Electroporation (IRE) Technology Globally
summary: Agreement combines Baird Medical's clinical, regulatory, and global commercialization expertise with Alpmed's leadership in IRE technology Collaboration will advance technology development, global regulatory approvals, commercialization, and clinical adoption across key international markets,
body_text: Baird Medical and Alpmed Enter Strategic Partnership to Advance Irreversible Electroporation (IRE) Technology Globally August 10, 2026 PDF Version Agreement combines Baird Medical's clinical, regulatory, and global commercialization expertise with Alpmed's leadership in IRE technology Collaboration will advance technology development, global regulatory approvals, commercialization, and clinical adoption across key international markets, including the United States NEW YORK, Aug. 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Baird Medical Investment Holdings Ltd. (NASDAQ: BDMD) (“Baird Medical” or the “Company”) and Tianjin Yuanshan Medical Technology Co., Ltd., operating under the Alpmed brand (“Alpmed”), a China-based innovator in irreversible electroporation (“IRE”) technology, announced the signing of a strategic cooperation agreement to establish a long-term partnership focused on global development and commercialization of next-generation IRE technologies. The partnership represents an important strategic milestone for Baird Medical, as the Company expands beyond its market-leading microwave ablation (MWA) system for benign thyroid nodules and broadens its portfolio of minimally invasive technologies targeting key markets worldwide. Under the partnership, the companies will initially collaborate on IRE, an advanced, non-thermal ablation technology that uses electrical pulses to destroy targeted tissue while preserving surrounding critical structures, such as blood vessels and nerves. The collaboration will combine Alpmed's expertise in IRE innovation with Baird Medical's regulatory and global commercialization capabilities, with the goal of advancing next-generation precision ablation solutions and exploring opportunities to expand the partnership beyond IRE. Baird Medical and Alpmed plan to submit a 510(k) application for the first co-developed product to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) by the end of 2026, with the potential to receive regulatory clearance in 2027. The first device is intended for the ablation of soft tissue solid tumors in the liver, breast, thyroid, and prostate. Baird Medical will lead the global regulatory approval processes, including in the U.S., and holds worldwide commercialization rights for this IRE product. "This partnership represents a significant milestone in Baird Medical's strategy to build a diversified global portfolio of innovative, minimally invasive treatment technologies," said Haimei Wu, Chairwoman and CEO of Baird Medical. "By combining Alpmed's leadership in irreversible electroporation with Baird Medical's proven regulatory and commercialization expertise, we believe we are well positioned to accelerate the global adoption of the jointly developed IRE technology. As we continue expanding our presence in the United States and other key international markets, this collaboration reinforces our long-term commitment to delivering differentiated technologies that create value for physicians, patients, and our shareholders." About Baird Medical Baird Medical is a global, pioneering medical device company specializing in minimally invasive ablation technologies for a range of solid tumors. The Company’s lead product, a microwave ablation (MWA) system, is FDA-cleared for soft tissue ablation and is being launched in the U.S. primarily for the treatment of benign thyroid nodules. In addition, the Company is expanding its minimally invasive technology portfolio, including IRE-based products and an AI-powered robotic ablation system. Baird Medical's MWA solutions have been adopted by over 30 leading U.S. institutions and private practice groups, including the Mayo Clinic, Columbia University Medical Center, UCSF Medical Center, and The George Washington University Hospital. The company is rapidly expanding its global commercial footprint, with sales now spanning more than 20 countries. About Alpmed Alpmed is a member company of Saixiang Group and is under common control with Tianjin Saixiang Technology Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 002337), a publicly listed company. Alpmed focuses on the research, development, and innovation of IRE technology and is an early mover and one of the leading companies in the field. The company has established an IRE technology portfolio across four areas: tumor ablation, cardiac electrophysiology, peripheral vascular intervention, and interventional pulmonology. In oncology, Alpmed has commercialized China’s first domestically developed IRE ablation product for malignant liver and pancreatic tumors. The company is also advancing applications of its technology in prostate, thyroid, breast, and other solid tumor indications. title: IT Nation Connect Global 2026: Flights, hotels, restaurants and travel tips
summary: Plan IT Nation Connect Global 2026 at Rosen Shingle Creek with hotel tips, MCO transportation, budgeting advice, and networking strategies.
body_text: IT Nation Connect Global 2026 brings the ConnectWise partner ecosystem together at Rosen Shingle Creek.[1] With a little planning before you arrive, you can head home with new ideas to improve your business, stronger vendor relationships, and practical advice from peers who have solved the same challenges. The right travel plan also makes it easier to focus on the conference instead of hotel logistics, expense reports, and other distractions. What is IT Nation Connect Global and who is it for? IT Nation Connect Global is ConnectWise's flagship gathering for managed service providers (MSPs) to share growth strategies, product roadmaps, and real-world experiences.[1] Whether you're evaluating new tools, refining service delivery, or looking for practical ways to grow your business, the conference combines product announcements, technical education, and peer networking in one place. The 2026 conference is expected to attract 4,000+ attendees for its 180+ sessions, 150+ speakers, and 130+ exhibitors.[1] You'll meet MSP owners evaluating acquisitions, operations leaders refining service delivery, sales and marketing leaders building pipeline, engineers evaluating security and automation platforms, and vendor partners meeting buyers on the show floor. IT Nation Connect Global is designed for the people who make technology and business decisions for MSPs. Role-based tracks span sales, marketing, service delivery, finance, and leadership alongside hands-on workshops and community programming throughout the event.[1] What makes IT Nation Connect Global 2026 worth the trip IT Nation Connect Global is as much about the conversations between sessions as the sessions themselves. Alongside ConnectWise product updates, you'll hear how other MSPs are approaching AI, cybersecurity, service delivery, hiring, and business growth. It's an opportunity to compare notes with peers, explore new vendors, and ask questions that don't always get answered in a webinar. Some of the highest-value experiences happen outside the breakout rooms: Solution Pavilion: Meet ConnectWise partners, compare products, watch live demonstrations, and connect with vendors serving the MSP community.[1] Workshops: Dive deeper into technical and business topics through hands-on sessions held throughout the conference.[1] Community Gathering: Meet other MSP professionals and connect with peers facing similar business and technology challenges.[1] PitchIT Competition: Watch emerging technology companies pitch their solutions to a panel of judges and the IT Nation community.[1] IT Nation Gives: Join the conference's community service event and network with other attendees while supporting a local cause.[1] Evening networking events: The Welcome Reception, IT Nation After Hours, the Pub Crawl, and the IT Nation Celebration provide opportunities to meet customers, partners, vendors, and fellow attendees outside formal sessions.[1] Getting the most out of IT Nation Connect Global starts before you arrive in Orlando. Planning your travel and conference schedule early leaves more time to focus on learning, networking, and the conversations that make the trip worthwhile. Where to stay for IT Nation Connect Global 2026 Rosen Shingle Creek is both the conference venue and the primary hotel, making it the most convenient place to stay. Nearby Rosen properties and International Drive hotels provide additional options if the official room block sells out or you prefer a different price point. Hotels near Rosen Shingle Creek in Orlando Compare hotel locations, travel times, and typical rates to choose the right option: Area Distance to venue Details Rates Rosen Shingle Creek 0–5 minutes walking Conference sessions, Solution Pavilion, and guest rooms in one resort complex Highest; book via registration confirmation link[2] Rosen Centre/Rosen Plaza Roughly 10 minutes on complimentary shuttle Sister Rosen properties on International Drive[2] Moderate; strong overflow option when Shingle Creek blocks fill up International Drive area 10–20 minutes by rideshare Hotels along I-Drive and Universal Blvd. have more open-market availability but no shuttle Lower to moderate; add commute time and surge pricing If staying onsite fits your budget, you'll be within walking distance of every session, networking event, and evening reception. Nearby Rosen properties offer convenient shuttle access, while International Drive hotels typically provide the widest range of prices if you're comfortable using rideshare. IT Nation Connect Global hotel pricing Navan analyzed anonymized hotel booking patterns in the area during the same week in 2025 to provide context for hotel pricing. Use these benchmarks while planning your trip: Median hotel rate: During conference week, the median nightly rate was $248 — roughly 11% higher than a typical September week near the venue ($223).[11] Stay length: Business travelers stayed an average of 2.9 nights.[11] Late bookings: Roughly 38% of bookings were made within two weeks of check-in.[11] Booking window: Travelers who booked 1–2 months ahead paid a median nightly rate of $211, while those who booked more than two months in advance paid a median nightly rate of $301.[11] If staying at Rosen Shingle Creek is your priority, book through the official ConnectWise hotel block as early as your travel policy allows. If rooms at Rosen Shingle Creek sell out, compare other Rosen properties nearby or International Drive hotels before booking elsewhere.[2] IT Nation Connect Global flight trends The primary airport serving IT Nation Connect Global 2026 is Orlando International Airport (MCO). Navan flight data from the same conference week in Orlando for 2025 showed there were 1,575 business flights into the city, with 8.4% from international origins.[11] The busiest origin cities were Minneapolis, Dallas-Fort Worth, Detroit, New York, and Salt Lake City.[11] If you're crossing time zones, consider arriving the day before the conference so you're well-rested and ready for opening day events. How Navan Edge helps you book your conference travel Use Navan Edge, your travel assistant powered by AI and 24/7 human travel experts, to plan and book your IT Nation Connect Global trip. Compare flights, hotels, and restaurants using live availability, personal preferences and the amenities you need , then combine and book everything in the same thread, without juggling multiple apps or websites. Continue earning your usual airline miles and hotel loyalty points, get your credit card points, and earn 5% back in Amazon Gift Cards on eligible hotel stays. If needed or wanted, human travel experts are available 24/7 to step into the same conversation thread with full context of your bookings and chat history. See our travel rewards on business trips guide for how it works. Set your Orlando budget before traveling The cost of attending IT Nation Connect Global goes well beyond airfare and accommodations. You have to account for your conference pass, MCO transfers, client dinners, and incidentals beyond what ConnectWise provides to conference attendees. Federal per diem for Orlando The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) sets federal per diem rates by city and season. At the time of publication, the following November rates for FY2026 applied to Orlando (Orange, Osceola, and Seminole counties): $220 per day combined: Includes $140 for nightly lodging plus $80 for daily meals and incidental expenses (M&IE) M&IE breakdown: Includes $20 for breakfast, $22 for lunch, $33 for dinner, and $5 for incidentals (reduce your meal allowance for any catering at the event)[5] First and last travel days: Includes M&IE allowance of $60 (i.e. 75% of the daily M&IE rate)[5] Updated rates for FY2027 (October 2026–September 2027) are expected to be published in mid-August 2026 at gsa.gov. During conference week, rooms at and around Rosen Shingle Creek often exceed the federal lodging rate, so budget for the difference or confirm with finance before booking.[11] Additional expenses Budgeting for these expenses before you travel can help you stay within policy, avoid last-minute surprises, and make your expense report easier to complete when you get home. Conference registration: An All-Access Pass starts at $900, with early-bird pricing of $700 through Sept. 25, 2026. Check the official event website for current rates.[4][5] Keynote & Solution Pavilion Pass: A pass starts at $350 and includes access to keynote sessions and the Solution Pavilion.[4] Social Guest Pass: A Social Guest Pass costs $350 and allows a non-attendee guest to join conference social events.[4] Team discount: Register two or more colleagues from the same company in one transaction to receive 25% off additional All-Access Passes.[2] Conference meals: Dinner at the Wednesday Welcome Reception plus breakfast, lunch, and dinner during conference events on Thursday and Friday are included with an All-Access Pass, so adjust your M&IE reimbursement accordingly.[2] Airport transfer: Expect to pay about $30–$50 for a rideshare from Orlando International Airport (MCO), $40–$60 for a taxi, or $15–$30 per person for a shared shuttle.[6][7] Client dinners: Private dining at A Land Remembered or Cala Bella typically costs $85–$200 per person before taxes, gratuity, and group minimums. After-hours networking: Leave room in your budget for partner receptions, team dinners, or other informal networking events beyond the conference schedule. Add up these costs before you buy so approvals and your post-trip expense report stay clean. Plan your IT Nation Connect Global 2026 agenda ConnectWise has published the agenda for IT Nation Connect Global 2026. Build your schedule around the sessions, meetings, and networking opportunities that best match your goals. Leave room for time in the Solution Pavilion, conversations with peers, and the unexpected introductions that often become the most valuable part of the conference. Here are some of the conference highlights: Wednesday (Nov. 4): Workshops, IT Nation Gives, the Community Gathering, the PitchIT Competition, the Welcome Keynote, the Welcome Reception, and IT Nation After Hours[1] Thursday (Nov. 5): The ConnectWise Product Keynote, the ThreatLocker Keynote, breakout sessions, the Solution Pavilion, the Pub Crawl, and the IT Nation Celebration[1] Friday (Nov. 6): Breakout sessions, the Solution Pavilion, the Guest Keynote, and the IT Nation Closing Reception[1] Build a plan based on priorities Start by reviewing the published agenda and identifying your highest-priority sessions. If you're traveling with colleagues, divide up overlapping sessions and compare notes afterward. Here are some tips to get ready for the event: Sessions: Save your must-attend sessions in the IT Nation Connect app and register for workshops or other limited-capacity events as soon as they become available.[1] Meetings: Reach out to customers, partners, vendors, or peers about two weeks before the conference to schedule a quick meeting while you're both onsite. Logistics: Download the IT Nation Connect app, enable session notifications, and set up your out-of-office auto-reply message. Contacts: Decide how you'll exchange contact information, whether that's LinkedIn, QR codes, or digital business cards, and jot down a quick note after each conversation so you remember the context later. Check out our business trip planning guide , covering flights, hotels, and departure checklists. What to pack and wear at IT Nation Connect Global Business casual is the norm at IT Nation Connect Global. Comfortable shoes are a must, especially if you'll be spending time in the Solution Pavilion, attending networking events, or walking across Rosen Shingle Creek's large resort campus. Orlando in November is mild and humid, with daytime highs around 80°F (27°C) and overnight lows near 60°F (16°C).[8] You'll move between air-conditioned ballrooms and outdoor walks across the resort grounds, so pack breathable daytime fabrics and a light layer for cold session rooms. Conference essentials A few small packing choices can make long days of sessions, meetings, and networking much more comfortable. Add these items to your suitcase before you leave: Two pairs of comfortable shoes: You'll spend a lot of time on your feet between sessions, the Solution Pavilion, networking events, and meetings across the resort. Portable charger: The conference app, note-taking, and networking can drain your phone before the day is over. Reusable water bottle: Staying hydrated is especially important if you're moving between outdoor walkways and warm November weather. Notebook or digital note-taking app: Capture ideas, vendor comparisons, and follow-up tasks while they're still fresh. Light sweater or zip-up: Meeting rooms are often much cooler than the outdoor temperatures. Getting from the airport to the IT Nation Connect Global venue Most attendees arrive for the conference at Orlando International Airport (MCO), roughly 12 miles from Rosen Shingle Creek.[6] For weekday business arrivals with checked bags, a rideshare or taxi is usually the fastest and easiest door-to-door choice. A little planning can make your arrival smoother, especially if you're landing during peak travel times. Option Time Cost Notes Rideshare (Uber/Lyft) 15–25 minutes $30–$50[6][7] Fastest door-to-door with pickup in designated rideshare zones; surge pricing during peak hours Taxi 15–25 minutes $40–$60[7] Curbside pickup and flat zone rates Shared shuttle 40–60 minutes $15–$30 per person[7] Lowest cost but longest travel time because of multiple hotel stops Beyond sessions: Make time for Solution Pavilion and networking It's tempting to fill every hour with breakout sessions, but some of the best conversations at IT Nation Connect Global happen in the Solution Pavilion, at networking events, and between sessions. Leave room in your schedule to explore, meet with vendors and partners, and connect with other MSP professionals. A few ways to plan your time: Set aside dedicated Solution Pavilion time: Don't try to squeeze vendor visits between sessions. Blocking time for demonstrations and conversations makes it easier to compare solutions and ask thoughtful questions. Schedule important meetings before you arrive: Reach out to customers, partners, or vendors a week or two before the conference so you're not coordinating calendars onsite. Leave room for networking: The Welcome Reception, IT Nation After Hours, the Pub Crawl, and other evening events offer additional opportunities to connect with peers and industry partners.[1] Take breaks throughout the day: A short walk, a coffee break, or a quiet moment between sessions can help you recharge and stay engaged through afternoon meetings and evening events. Capture your next steps: Jot down a few notes after each conversation so it's easier to follow up once you're back at the office. Where to eat at IT Nation Connect Global 2026 Most of your conference meals are covered with an All-Access Pass, including the Wednesday Welcome Reception and meals served during conference events on Thursday and Friday.[2] Packing a protein bar or other easy snack is also a good idea in case you find yourself heading straight from a breakout session to the Solution Pavilion without much downtime. You'll also want to plan for client dinners, coffee meetings, and the occasional meal between sessions. Here are a few good dining options at Rosen Shingle Creek: Client dinners: A Land Remembered offers Florida-inspired cuisine and handles executive steakhouse dinners with the MacIvey private dining room for up to 24 guests.[9] Team meals: Cala Bella serves Italian and Mediterranean fine dining, with a private room that seats up to 42 for group celebrations and partner dinners.[10] Quick fuel: Café Osceola offers a full American buffet for breakfast and lunch, while Tobias Burgers & Brews and 18 Monroe Street Market are faster casual options on property.[12] One-on-one or small groups: Banrai Sushi and Mi Casa Tequila Taquería are great for smaller meetings, with flexible seating and shorter service times than formal private dining.[12] If you need help booking a restaurant, Navan Edge can reserve restaurants in Orlando in the same chat where you arranged your hotel and flights. Finish strong on departure day Your time at IT Nation Connect Global isn't over when the closing reception ends. Before you head home, take a few minutes to wrap up the week and set yourself up for an easier return to work. Pack the night before: Charge your devices, set aside your travel clothes, and check the room for chargers, conference swag, and anything else you may have left behind. Confirm your checkout time: If you need a little extra time before heading to MCO, request a late checkout at the front desk or let Navan Edge coordinate it for you. Leave extra time for the airport: MCO is a busy airport, so plan to arrive at least two hours before a domestic flight or three hours before an international departure. Submit your expenses while they're fresh: Upload receipts before they disappear into your backpack, and complete your expense report before you're back in the flow of everyday work. Follow up with new contacts: Send a quick email or LinkedIn message to the people you met while the conversations are still fresh in everyone's mind. title: Post-Award Grant Management: A Practical Guide for Grantmakers
summary: Grantmakers know that the post-award phase is where a lot of the high-stakes work happens. Here's how to get post-award grant management right.
body_text: Grant managers know that the work doesn’t stop once a grant is awarded. In fact, the post-award phase is where a lot of the high-stakes work happens. The post-award phase is when grantmakers follow through on the promise of their grant program. It’s when applicants become true partners. But the right processes have to be in place to make those relationships successful. What is post-award grant management? Post-award grant management is the final stage of the grant management process . It’s everything that happens once the grant is awarded, all the way through closeout. Financial oversight is a big component of the post award process. Grantmakers need to have clear workflows to move funds into grantees' hands. This includes reimbursements, clear budget tracking, and spend down processes. Alongside the financial monitoring, reporting is also a big focus in this phase of the grant lifecycle. Grantees might need to submit progress reports or hit specific milestones to show that they’re holding up their end and meeting compliance regulations. Though it’s easy to think about the post-award phase as a checklist, that doesn’t quite capture the full depth of the work during this stage. Every decision you make about your post-award process shapes your relationship with your grantees. It’s essential to handle each one with care. Post-award best practices to make compliance easy Some of the biggest news stories about grant programs focus on when things go catastrophically wrong in the post-award phase. Take the case of the one million dollars diverted from the Margaret A. Cargill Foundation or the estimated $9 billion in fraud in Minnesota’s DHS programs. The risks of getting things wrong are high. What you don’t often hear about are the quieter challenges in the post-award phase—the mismatched expectations and frayed relationships that happen when processes get off track. Though not as newsworthy, these can also undercut the work you’re trying to do. Here’s how to get your post-award workflow right. Approach the process from a partnership lens View every step of the grant lifecycle from the grantee perspective. Imagine if you were the one tasked with moving through the post-award phase as a grantee. Identify any repetitive requests or confusing steps. Create a process that respects their time, ensures transparency, and provides clarity. Set up expectations both ways Your award agreement acts as a map for your grant partnerships. The agreement should lay out expectations and timelines so everyone knows what’s coming and there aren’t surprises along the way. If your award agreement doesn’t provide this structure, you might find yourself chasing down progress reports and receipts as deadlines approach, and setting up your grantees for the same kind of frantic scramble. Make space for mutual flexibility Clear expectations are important for strong partnerships. So is flexibility. You don’t want to feel like your award agreement structure is so rigid that you can’t make changes when you or your grantee needs to. It’s best to have a clear plan that includes a process for making changes as the need arises. 11 of the most important post-award features in your grant management software Though your whole post-award process can’t be boiled down to a single checklist, you need the right feature in your GMS to keep partnerships on track. Look for full lifecycle support with these features. A single portal: One portal with an organization login allows a grantee to have their whole team involved in ways that make sense for each role. Customizable award agreement : The award agreement can’t be a one-size-fits-all. It should be unique to each grantee and connect to upcoming goals, milestones, and reports. Amendments: Amendments allow you to easily make changes to the award agreement with an automatic digital record for compliance and transparency. ‍ Goals and milestone tracking: Goals and milestones help you stay on the same page with grantees. The award agreement should map them out with expectations and timelines. Budget visibility : Budget tracking should update in real time and give grantees and admins their own access to the same dashboard. ‍ Ability to define budget categories : You should be able to create budget categories and use automatic indirect cost calculations. ‍ Expense tracking and reimbursements : Reimbursements should be quick and easy with automated invoice generation. ‍ Progress reports: Scheduleable progress reports ensure you don’t have to manually keep up or chase down grantees. ‍ Disbursement schedule: Disbursements should link to milestones, so funds are released as soon as grantees submit their reports and receipts. ‍ Flexible payment options: Whether grantees need ACH, prepaid card, or something else, your GMS should provide the right options. ‍ Built-in Docusign integration: Know that contracts are secure and hassle-free with a built-in Docusign integration. Your GMS sets everyone up for success How you construct your post-award process can make or break the effectiveness and resilience of your grant programs. If you’re looking for a new grant management software, be sure to choose one that has all the features to create and maintain strong partnerships. title: CRM Integration for AI Proposal Tools in GovCon (August 2026)
summary: Learn how GovCon teams connect Salesforce capture intelligence to AI proposal tools for faster, stronger federal bids in August 2026.
body_text: Most GovCon teams running Salesforce or HubSpot have more capture intelligence stored in their CRM than ever makes it into a proposal draft. The gap between that pipeline data and your proposal workflow is where things break down, and the decision to integrate AI with your Salesforce CRM in Government Contracting is what determines whether your BD investment carries forward or resets at kickoff. TLDR: CRM intelligence built during pre-RFP capture often stays locked in Salesforce or HubSpot records and never reaches the proposal workspace where it matters. AI proposal tools connected to your CRM can pre-populate Section L responses, cross-reference past performance against Section M criteria, and pull bid/no-bid signals like PWin scores directly from CRM opportunity records. HubSpot is not FedRAMP authorized; teams tracking CUI through it need to confirm data boundaries before connecting any AI proposal tool. When assessing integration depth, ask vendors whether the tool recognizes GovCon-specific fields like NAICS codes and incumbent data by default, and whether attaching a solicitation to an opportunity record automatically triggers proposal section population. In practice, GovCon teams using a CRM-connected AI proposal tool have cut Gate 0 decision time from days to hours and pursued an average of two additional RFPs per month without adding headcount. Why GovCon BD Teams Run on Salesforce and HubSpot GovCon BD teams gravitate toward Salesforce and HubSpot for the same reason capture managers obsess over pipeline visibility: federal pursuit cycles are long, and contact relationships decay faster than most CRMs are configured to track. A single IDIQ opportunity can involve agency contacts, teaming partners, incumbent research, and bid/no-bid checkpoints spread across 18 to 36 months. Generic CRM setups were not built for that kind of pursuit cadence. Salesforce dominates at larger primes and mid-tier contractors where BD and Contracts teams need shared pipeline views, custom opportunity stages tied to capture phases, and integrations with procurement data feeds. HubSpot has gained ground at smaller firms and growth-stage 8(a) or SDVOSB contractors who need structured capture pipeline tracking without the configuration investment that full Salesforce deployments typically require for GovCon-specific field mapping. Both systems end up holding the intelligence that drives proposal decisions: agency relationship history, teaming partner contacts, prior capture notes, and bid history with past-performance data. The gap most pursuit teams hit is that this intelligence stays locked inside CRM records and never connects to the proposal workflow where it would actually reduce Section L response time or sharpen past-performance selection. The Capture-to-Proposal Intelligence Gap Most GovCon CRM environments hold more capture intelligence than any proposal team ever retrieves. Contacts, call notes, incumbent data, and past-performance references accumulate in Salesforce or HubSpot records, then sit disconnected from the proposal workspace when an RFP drops. The result: writers pull from memory or shared drives instead of the structured intelligence the BD team spent months building. That gap is where proposals lose coherence before the first draft is written. AI proposal tools that integrate with Salesforce and HubSpot close this by pulling CRM data directly into the drafting environment, so the capture context follows the opportunity instead of staying behind in a CRM record no one opens under deadline. Initiate Government Solutions (IGS) , a federal IT services provider, saw that gap close in practice; after connecting their BD workflow to GovEagle, Gate 0 decisions that previously took days dropped to hours, and the team was able to pursue an average of two additional RFPs per month. What CRM Integration with an AI Proposal Tool Actually Does When a GovCon team connects an AI proposal tool to Salesforce or HubSpot, the integration does more than sync contact records. Capture data that previously sat in CRM notes, including incumbent intel, agency relationships, past-performance tags, and historical PWin scores , becomes active input for AI-generated proposal drafts, win themes, and compliance matrices. The practical result is that proposal writers stop re-entering context that BD already captured. Section L requirements get mapped against pursuit history pulled directly from the CRM record. Win themes drafted by the AI reflect the actual account intelligence logged by capture managers, not generic boilerplate. For GovCon teams running multiple pursuits simultaneously, that connection between CRM activity and proposal output can reduce the coordination overhead that typically consumes time between capture close and proposal kickoff. Key Capabilities Unlocked by CRM-Connected AI Proposal Tools When a CRM like Salesforce or HubSpot feeds directly into an AI proposal tool, the integration does more than cut down on copy-paste work. It changes what capture teams can act on and when. A few capabilities tend to matter most in practice. Opportunity data pulled from Salesforce or HubSpot can pre-populate proposal sections automatically, drawing on incumbent details, contract vehicle history, and agency relationship notes that BD teams have already logged during pre-RFP capture activities. AI tools connected to CRM pipelines can cross-reference past performance records stored in the CRM against Section M evaluation criteria, surfacing which prior contracts are worth citing before the writing even starts. Bid/no-bid scoring can draw on CRM signals like PWin estimates, incumbent status flags, and relationship depth scores, giving capture leads earlier visibility into whether a pursuit is worth resourcing. Account intel logged in the CRM, including agency relationship notes, teaming partner history, and prior contract data, can feed directly into win theme generation and capture deck population, so the intelligence the BD team built during pre-RFP pursuit carries into proposal development without manual re-entry. The practical result is that intelligence captured during the pursuit phase stops living only in CRM notes and starts feeding the proposal directly. That matters in GovCon because the gap between what a capture team learns about an agency and what actually makes it into a proposal draft is often where competitive differentiation gets lost. How to Assess CRM Integration Depth When Selecting an AI Proposal Tool When a GovCon team reviews AI proposal tools, CRM integration is often treated as a checkbox, not a structural criterion. That framing leads to a common procurement mistake: selecting a tool that "connects" to Salesforce or HubSpot in name but leaves capture intelligence siloed the moment proposal workflows begin. Integration depth matters more than integration existence. A few areas where the distinction shows up most clearly: Integration Criterion Shallow Integration Deep Integration Data Flow Directionality Manual or unreliable pull: capture data must be copied into the proposal workspace by hand at kickoff, creating gaps when notes are incomplete or the CRM record is out of date Reliable inbound pull: capture intelligence, opportunity stage data, and account history from CRM records flow into the proposal workspace automatically when a pursuit goes active, so proposal teams start with the full pursuit context the BD team built Field Mapping Maps to standard Salesforce or HubSpot objects only; NAICS codes, vehicle types, and incumbent data are not recognized Maps to GovCon-specific custom fields, preserving the capture intelligence your BD team has already built, including incumbent data, vehicle history, and agency relationship history Trigger-Based Automation Passive connection; capture data must be manually pulled into the proposal workspace at kickoff Attaching a solicitation to an opportunity record auto-populates Section L compliance matrix requirements, removing the manual handoff that introduces errors or delays Before committing to a tool, ask vendors directly how reliably capture intelligence flows from CRM records into the proposal workspace, what GovCon-specific field mappings come preconfigured, and whether workflow triggers can be customized to your capture stages. GovEagle: Closing the Loop Between Salesforce and Proposal Execution Most CRM integrations stop at data sync. A contact record updates, a tag fires, an opportunity stage advances. The proposal workflow stays exactly where it was: in a separate tool, a shared drive, or someone's inbox. GovEagle is built to close that gap. When a Salesforce opportunity reaches a configured capture threshold, GovEagle can pull the relevant BD intelligence directly into the proposal workspace, including incumbent data, teaming notes, agency history, and win themes developed during pre-RFP capture activities , without requiring the proposal manager to hunt across systems. What That Looks Like in Practice Capture leads update opportunity records in Salesforce as intelligence develops. When a pursuit moves to active proposal, GovEagle reads those records and pulls the relevant BD intelligence into the proposal workspace, so the process starts with real capture context, not a blank template. The account history, agency notes, and win themes the BD team built during pre-RFP capture become the starting point for proposal development, not artifacts that stay locked in the CRM. Book a Demo to see how that handoff works across live pursuits in your pipeline. For GovCon teams managing simultaneous pursuits across multiple contract vehicles, that inbound connection matters. Proposal managers get structured capture input at the moment they need it, with the pursuit intelligence the BD team built already loaded into the workspace when the proposal kicks off. Security and Deployment Context GovEagle is FedRAMP authorized and supports AWS GovCloud and Azure self-hosted deployments. For teams handling CUI within their proposal or CRM workflows, the integration architecture aligns with NIST 800-171 requirements , which matters given that DFARS 252.204-7012 safeguarding obligations remain in force regardless of the current CMMC Phase II suspension. FAQs What does "integration depth" mean for a Salesforce-connected AI proposal tool in government contracting? Integration depth refers to whether the connection between your CRM and your AI proposal tool moves capture intelligence into active use or just syncs records. The practical tests are pull reliability (does capture intelligence flow automatically into the proposal workspace when a pursuit goes active, or does someone have to manually pull it across?), field mapping (does the tool recognize GovCon-specific fields like NAICS codes, vehicle types, and incumbent flags?), and trigger-based automation (does attaching an RFP to an opportunity automatically populate Section L requirement mappings?). Should I integrate my AI proposal tool with Salesforce Government Cloud or standard Salesforce if my team handles CUI? Salesforce Government Cloud offerings are designed to support organizations with FedRAMP and federal compliance requirements. Teams handling CUI under DFARS 252.204-7012 should verify that both their Salesforce environment and any connected AI tools meet their contractual security obligations. The configuration difference matters for AI tool connections too: GovCloud uses separate API endpoints, so AI proposal tools built against the standard Salesforce API may require a purpose-built connector to authenticate correctly. Can I connect HubSpot to an AI proposal tool for federal pursuits, or does HubSpot's lack of FedRAMP authorization block the integration? HubSpot integrations are feasible for federal proposal workflows, but the data boundary requires deliberate scoping since HubSpot is not FedRAMP authorized , which means teams should confirm that CUI stays out of HubSpot records or is handled through a compliant intermediary before connecting any AI proposal tool to it. Where HubSpot works well is syncing opportunity stage data, BD call logs, and pre-RFP engagement notes into proposal context for past-performance and management approach sections, as long as the data involved does not cross into controlled territory. Final Thoughts on Using AI to Bridge CRM Data and Proposal Execution Most BD teams are already sitting on more pursuit intelligence than their proposal teams ever see. The problem is not the data; it is that Salesforce and HubSpot records and the proposal workspace are two separate systems with no live connection between them. Teams that integrate AI with their Salesforce CRM in Government Contracting close that gap, so capture context feeds the Section L response framework from day one instead of getting reconstructed from memory.

body_text: View All News National 811 Day: Damaging Underground Utility Lines During Digging Can be a Serious Public Safety Issue August 10, 2026 A Free Call to 811 Will Help Keep You Safe and Avoid Expensive Repairs OAKLAND, Calif. , Aug. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Most every day, somewhere in Pacific Gas and Electric's (PG&E) service area in Northern and Central California, an underground utility line is damaged due to digging. Each of these incidents pose a public safety risk requiring a 911 response and can result in repair bills averaging $3,500. To help prevent these incidents and to raise awareness of the importance of calling 811 before any digging project, large or small, Tuesday, August 11 is recognized as National 811 Day. Not contacting 811 before digging is the top driver of damages to buried utilities every year. In PG&E's service area alone, there were over 1,200 line strikes during 2025, and in 55% of these incidents, 811 was not called. Underground utility lines can be shallow, sometimes only a few inches below the surface, so it is important to call 811 before any project that involves digging, even for seemingly small projects like building or replacing a fence, planting and landscaping. "By making a fast and free call to 811, utility professionals will come to your home or job site and mark the location of underground lines so that you can dig safely and avoid expensive repairs. Know what's below before you start any size digging project, whether you are planting, landscaping, or doing fence work and call 811 two days before you dig. Remember, call 811 so that you don't have to call 911," said Mitch Smith, Director, PG&E Damage Prevention. By the Numbers Warmer weather months see an increase in digging projects and a corresponding increase in the number of strikes to underground lines that have not been marked ahead of time. In fact, throughout PG&E's service area of Northern and Central California: There were 1,247 incidents during 2025 in PG&E's service area where underground utility lines were damaged due to digging, and in 55% of incidents when an underground utility line was damaged due to digging, 811 was not called So far in 2026, there have been 561 incidents where underground utility lines were damaged due to digging, and in 57% of incidents when an underground utility line was damaged due to digging, 811 was not called. For homeowners specifically, that percentage rises to 89% The average cost to repair a damaged utility line is $3,500 Leading causes of damages to underground utility lines while digging include: building or replacing a fence, gardening and landscaping, planting a tree or removing a stump, sewer and irrigation work and building a deck or patio When a call is placed to 811 and a request is made to have lines located and marked, a professional locator will come to your project site to mark the location of underground utility lines, including gas, electric, water, telecom and sewer, free of charge. Knowing where underground lines are buried while you are digging and following safe digging practices will help keep you and your family safe and connected to essential utility services. Calling 811 is Fast and Free Customers should call 811 a minimum of two business days before beginning any project that involves digging, no matter how large or small. Customers also can visit USANCA - OneCallAccess to have underground utility lines marked for their project site. Professional utility workers for all utilities (gas, electric, water, sewer and telecommunications) will be dispatched to mark the location of all underground utility lines for the project site with flags, spray paint, or both The 811 call center serving Northern and Central California, USA North, is staffed 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and will provide Spanish and other translation services. PG&E Safe Digging Tips Mark project area in white: Identify the digging location by drawing a box around the area using white paint, white stakes, white flags, white chalk or even white baking flour. Call 811 or submit an online request a minimum of two working days before digging: Be prepared to provide the address and general location of the project, project start date and type of digging activity. PG&E and other utilities will identify underground facilities in the area for free. Requests can be submitted a maximum of 14 days prior to the start of the project. Dig safely: Use hand tools when digging within 24 inches of the outside edge of underground lines. Leave utility flags, stakes or paint marks in place until the project is finished. Backfill and compact the soil. Be aware of signs of a natural gas leak: Smell for a "rotten egg" odor, listen for hissing, whistling or roaring sounds and look for dirt spraying into the air, bubbling in a pond or creek and dead/dying vegetation in an otherwise moist area. If you smell gas, call 911 and then call PG&E at 800-743-5000.
